Revolution(s ) is an exciting play, set in Chicago and fueled with the political activism and musical spirit of Morello, cofounder of Rage Against the Machine, and the writing talent of Dohrn, son of 1960s Chicago radicals.

Cogent, assertive, unapologetic, the score for this galvanizing musical about family and legacy, oppression and resistance comes courtesy of composer/lyricist Tom Morello, Libertyville’s famously, fiercely political musician/activist who co-founded Rage Against the Machine and Audioslave.
Revolution(s) enthralling music and provocative narrative is a good place to start, and they are ready to help you.
As a concert production, Morello’s cri de coeur against social and racial injustice would be a rousing, pulsating success.
Revolution(s) is a new rock musical that tells a story of generations of radical activists.
Revolution(s) makes a powerful debut at the Goodman Theatre, uniting personal history with political urgency in a way that feels both intimate and explosive.
I will tell you that there are a few places where you might forget that you are at a play, feeling like this could be a concert and you will see yourself clapping your hands along witht he ensemble.

cn.t: Critics find this punk-rock musical about generational activism timely and electrifying, praising Morello's propulsive score and high-energy performances, though some feel the rebellious spirit gets lost in the noise.
